observed_result.criterion: Race of a client connect against ssh -O stop with randomized start delays (client 0-60 ms, stop 0-40 ms by default; see run knobs) (client cannot authenticate, so rc 0 means admitted through the master): 0 admissions of clients that started after the -O stop call had returned (MUX_S_OK received). Admissions of clients that overlapped the stop call cannot be ordered from the host and are reported separately. Validity precondition: at least 5 clients started after the stop call returned.
observed_result.summary: Observed: 50 iterations, each a fresh master (ControlPersist=3 s) racing a client that cannot authenticate (PubkeyAuthentication=no) against ssh -O stop, start delays uniform client 0-60 ms / stop 0-40 ms. -O stop rc 0 in 50/50. 25 clients started after the stop call had returned: 0 admitted (all 25 went to a fresh connection and were refused with publickey denial). 7 clients overlapped the stop call: 1 admitted, 6 refused. 18 clients started before the stop call: all 18 admitted. All 50 masters exited on their own within ControlPersist+5 s. Server Accepted lines = 50 = masters (no client authenticated itself). Verdict pass against the stated criterion (no admission of a client that STARTED after stop returned). This criterion cannot detect admissions on control connections accepted before the listener closed; such admissions occur (G09-prelim-mux-preconnected-after-stop), and the admitted overlapping client is consistent with that. The race does not show that -O stop stops admissions.

No Heimdall code exists or ran; this is not evidence of Heimdall behavior.

Not desktop-lock, sleep, logout, reboot or secure-store evidence: the dedicated agents are plain ssh-agent processes in an unlocked session started by the harness. Lock continuity remains open (owner-run probes).
Single machine: macOS 27.0 arm64 with Docker Desktop (linux VM). No native Windows/WSL or Linux-host evidence. The openssh-server package version is observed, not pinned (apt floats at image build).
Fixture sshd sets PerSourcePenalties no, unlike the OpenSSH 10 default.
Requirement IDs are listed for traceability; this record is not by itself evidence that any product requirement is met (tests/evidence/README.md).

Independent review M00-review-g04 (tests/evidence/artifacts/m00-wf2/review-g04.json) re-ran the earlier version of these experiments from scratch and refuted the earlier '-O stop: admissions stopped' conclusion; this record comes from the corrected harness (task M00-T04-G04-fix). The corrections themselves have not been independently re-reviewed.

Host-side millisecond timestamps include process start overhead; the instant the -O stop client receives MUX_S_OK is not observable from outside, so admissions of clients that started while the stop call was in flight are reported separately and not counted as violations.
Small sample (N=50 by default), single host, masters without other sessions; not a proof of absence of a race, only of none observed.

Classification is by client process start time. A client whose control connection the master accepted before the listener closed is a pre-accepted connection, and such connections are admitted after MUX_S_OK (G09-prelim-mux-preconnected-after-stop); admissions classed started_during_stop are consistent with that. The race criterion therefore cannot show that -O stop stops admissions; it shows only that clients that started after stop returned found no listener.
